summary: Both sides rise a warm sun from the bottom edge to grid centre inside an ember halo at matching radii, but the port's sun is a tiny, dim, perfectly static blob (peak 77, radius ~2 px) where the original's is a large, textured, hollow-cored disc (peak ~250, radius ~5 px) that flares and rotates on a ~4.4 s cycle.
observations: Rig: 16x16 grid, 256 px. Neither side has a compile or runtime error on the default rig; neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both). Both sides are completely wall-clock independent: --wall-clock sweeps at 1755978000 / 1756000000 / 1756021200 / 1756042800 produced identical stats on both sides, so the known time-of-day engine gap does NOT apply to this pair and everything below is directly comparable.

SHARED, CORRECT BEHAVIOUR — the sunrise itself. Both sides start black, a warm disc appears near the bottom edge and translates upward to grid centre, then holds. Core centroid (radius<=5.5 weighted, 16x16): orig (8.1, 11.0) at t=1 -> (8.0, 5.9) at t=3; port (7.3, 11.7) at t=3 -> (7.3, 7.3) at t=6. Same start position, same final height, same direction. Port's rise starts ~2 s later and takes ~2x as long (orig fully risen by t~2-3 s, port by t~6 s).

SHARED, CORRECT — the ember/spark halo. Sparse orange dots orbit outside the sun on both sides at the SAME radii: mean spark radius 7.05 px on both, range r=6.0..9.9 (orig) vs 6.0..9.3 (port), measured over 15 dumps in the 100-128 s steady window. Palette family matches: meanB is exactly 0 on both sides in every run; spark R/G ratio 4.67 (orig) vs 4.02 (port).

DIVERGENCE 1 — sun size and shape. Steady-state radial profile (mean max-channel per integer radius, 16x16, r=1..8): orig peaks at r=3-5 with a HOLLOW core, e.g. t=106 s [r1=5, r2=7, r3=35, r4=79, r5=56, r6=8]; port is a solid centred gaussian [r1=46, r2=20, r3=6, r4=1, r5~0]. Orig's disc spans cols 3-12 / rows 3-12 (diameter ~10 px); port's spans cols 6-8 / rows 6-8 (diameter ~3 px). Confirmed resolution-independent: re-rendered at --grid 48x48 the same normalised profiles hold (orig peak at r/W ~0.25 with a dim core; port peak at r=0), so this is a real shape difference, not a rig/aliasing artefact.

DIVERGENCE 2 — the sun body is frozen on the port. Over 15 dumps spanning 100-128 s the port's core radial profile is [46,20,6,1] on EVERY frame (peak pixel pinned at exactly 77 every single time), while the orig's core mean swings 18->92 and its peak pixel swings 127->252. A 5 s / 20 fps dump at t=120-125 s isolates this: orig core mean 52.8 -> 92.4 -> 35.3 -> 70.0 within 5 s; port core mean stays 6.7-8.5 the whole time, and every non-zero pixel delta on the port comes from sparks passing through the core radius, not from the disc.

DIVERGENCE 3 — no flare rhythm on the port. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness over the 100-130 s window at 10 fps: orig has a strong peak at lag 44 frames = 4.4 s (r=0.90) with std 2.71 on mean 10.83 (~25% swing) — the disc's bright limb sweeps around the ring on that period; port's best non-trivial lag is 12 frames = 1.2 s at only r=0.47 with std 0.44 on mean 2.88, which is just spark churn. Visually (ASCII/dump inspection at 4 s spacing) the orig's disc has moving bright arcs, dark spots and a rotating hot limb; the port's is a smooth, texture-free gaussian.

DIVERGENCE 4 — overall brightness. 500 s / 2 fps survey: orig meanBrightness avg 11 (range 5-16 after settling), port avg 3 (range 2-4). Peak pixel: orig 127-252 across the steady window, port pinned at 77. The port is roughly 3.5-4x too dim overall and 3x too dim at peak.

DIVERGENCE 5 — spark density. Steady window, pixels at r>5.8 with max-channel >=20: orig 7.7 per frame (median value 86, max 127), port 15.1 per frame (median 53, max 77). The port has about twice as many embers and each is about 40% dimmer. Combined with the tiny sun, the sparks are the dominant visual element on the port whereas the sun dominates on the original.

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes one slider named 'sliderMakeTheSunRise' (label 'MakeTheSunRise'); the port exposes one slider named 'sliderMakeTheSunRiseAgain' (label 'MakeTheSunRiseAgain'). Same count and same kind, but the NAME differs, so a saved-value restore or any external control by name would not reach the port's dial.

Off-default-rig note (not a headline): at --grid 8x8 the ORIGINAL dies with 'array index out of bounds' (runtime error, renders black) while the port renders fine. That is an original-side limitation on a rig it was never given, recorded only for completeness; all judging above is on the default 16x16 grid, cross-checked at 48x48.
Seed independence: --seed 7 and --seed 1234 over the 100-120 s window reproduce the same stats as seed 1 on BOTH sides (orig mean 11, port mean 3-4), so none of the above is a one-seed fluke.
Untouched-default divergence is the same divergence as the dialed one — every dialed run reproduces the observations above unchanged.

dials.name: sliderMakeTheSunRise (orig) / sliderMakeTheSunRiseAgain (port)
dials.origEffect: Value-inert but setter-sensitive. An 8-value sweep (0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 1) over a 8 s / 10 fps window at --skip 60 produced BYTE-IDENTICAL frame dumps for all eight values (same sha256, same pixel sum 28518). Merely calling the setter does perturb the pattern — the untouched render over the same window hashes differently (sum 27872), matching the probe's uniform maxDelta of 8.49 at all three probe values — so setting the slider restarts/reseeds something, but the VALUE has no effect. Dial effect therefore unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Fully inert: the same 8-value sweep AND the untouched render all hash identically (sum 5541) — neither the value nor the setter call changes anything. Probe maxDelta 0.00 at 0/0.5/1, confirmed by hand over an 8 s multi-flare window at t=60 s and by 60 s / 5 fps runs at 0/0.5/1 (mean 2 in all three).

feedback: The sun disc is far too small. On a 16x16 grid the original's disc spans ~10 px across (radial brightness peaks at r=3-5 and reaches r=6); the port's reaches only r=2 and is essentially gone by r=4. Scale the disc radius up by roughly 2.5x. The size law is in normalised coordinates on both sides (verified at 48x48), so fix the radius constant, not the rasterisation.

The original's disc is HOLLOW/annular, not a filled gaussian: its radial profile dips at the centre (r=1 as low as 5 while r=4 is 79) at least half the time. The port draws a monotonically-decaying centred blob (46, 20, 6, 1). Give the disc a bright rim/limb with a darker interior rather than a peak-at-centre falloff.

The port's sun body is completely static once risen — its radial profile is bit-identical on every frame from t=6 s to t=500 s and its peak pixel is pinned at exactly 77. The original's disc is turbulent: bright arcs, dark spots, and a hot limb that sweeps around, driving a ~4.4 s brightness cycle (autocorr r=0.90 at lag 44 frames @10 fps) with the whole-rig mean swinging 5-16. Whatever noise/turbulence/rotation term drives that on the original is missing or has zero amplitude on the port.

Brightness is ~3.5-4x too low. Target whole-rig meanBrightness ~11 in steady state (port currently 3) and a peak pixel around 220-250 (port currently capped at 77). The port never produces a yellow highlight: the original's hottest pixels run to [225,152,0] and [218,227,0] (yellow/white-hot), the port's hottest is [60,12,0] / value 77 (deep orange). Extend the palette's top end into yellow.

Ember halo density is about 2x too high and each ember ~40% too dim: original averages 7.7 sparks per frame with median brightness 86, port averages 15.1 with median 53 (measured at r>5.8, threshold 20, over the 100-128 s steady window on the default 16x16 rig). The halo RADIUS distribution is already correct (mean r=7.05 on both) — only count and brightness need adjusting.

The rise transient is ~2x too slow and starts ~2 s late: the original's sun is off the bottom edge by t~1 s and fully risen by t~2-3 s; the port's first appears at t~3 s and settles at t~6 s. Same path and same final height, so only the ramp rate/onset delay needs changing.
Rename the port's control from 'sliderMakeTheSunRiseAgain' to the original's 'sliderMakeTheSunRise' — same kind and count, but the differing name breaks name-keyed control restore.
Neither side's slider is value-responsive from output (all values byte-identical on both), so no dial behaviour can be verified here; this is a caveat, not permission to change the control surface.
